title: Reliability in Educational Measurement
relevance: Current authoritative fifth-edition chapter; connects GT to CTT/IRT and precision of reliability estimates.
evidence: Full text acquired; read GT overview, Error in Reliability Estimates (printed pp.360–361), practical guidelines and bibliography. Not a complete reading of its 105 pages. Simulations/resampling omit some replication error; few sampled levels make GT component estimates uncertain.
acquisition_note: NCME official chapter posted January 2026; original citation 2025. Acquisition validated by scripts/acquire.py; source sidecar contains timestamp, bytes and SHA-256.

title: Empirical Investigation of Various Reliability Statistics
relevance: CASMA 58 companion computations for fifth-edition chapter, valuable formulas/tables for reference comparisons.
evidence: Full text acquired; read introduction, single-domain/composite coefficient comparisons, computational tools and conclusions. Pseudo-parallel half forms preserve content/statistics and use one occasion: benchmark captures item sampling while occasion/motivation/context held constant. Coefficient alpha equals single-facet GT G; composite stratification changes results.
acquisition_note: December 2025 (PDF/index verified); 25 PDF pages. Computational examples are not interval-coverage validation. Acquisition validated by scripts/acquire.py; source sidecar contains timestamp, bytes and SHA-256.

title: The Bootstrap and Other Procedures for Examining the Variability of Estimated Variance Components in Testing Contexts
relevance: Original GT resampling investigation and finite-universe jackknife formulas.
evidence: Full text acquired; read summary/conclusions pp.24–27, AppendixB jackknife/pseudo-values, finite universe tables and bootstrap comparisons. Normal/binary p×i simulations; component-dependent bootstrap recommendations. AppendixB includes c_n=1−n/N and c_k=1−k/K and corrects Cronbach 1972 extra sqrt(nk) divisor. Different conclusions for jackknife than later studies.
acquisition_note: ACT report 87-7 September 1987, iii+53 pages; OCR formulas require visual confirmation before implementation. Acquisition validated by scripts/acquire.py; source sidecar contains timestamp, bytes and SHA-256.

title: Bootstrap Procedures for Estimating Standard Errors of Estimated Variance Components for Two-Facet Designs
relevance: CASMA 5 original two-facet normal-data bootstrap study.
evidence: Full text acquired; read methods/designs, conclusions and appendix bias factors. p×i×h and p×(i:h), particular 100×20×2 normal-data structure. Tentative rules and explicit future extension to dichotomous/polytomous data.
acquisition_note: February 2004; precursor to later 2006/2007 work, not independent corroboration. Acquisition validated by scripts/acquire.py; source sidecar contains timestamp, bytes and SHA-256.

title: Bootstrap Techniques for Estimating Variability in Generalizability Theory
relevance: CASMA 15 extends to normal/dichotomous/polytomous crossed and nested designs.
evidence: Full text acquired; read methods, correction formulas and discussion. 1000 trials and 100 bootstrap draws/trial,100×20×2 design. Main effects use own-facet bootstrap; interactions largest-sample facet. Boot-p works for SE(relative error); no bootstrap performed well for SE(absolute error). Ad hoc correction formulas explicitly lack rigorous derivation in this report.
acquisition_note: March 2006 report. Final 2007 article uses Brennan unbiased procedures; do not conflate versions. Acquisition validated by scripts/acquire.py; source sidecar contains timestamp, bytes and SHA-256.

title: Unbiased Estimates of Variance Components with Bootstrap Procedures: Detailed Results
relevance: General derivations replacing ad hoc bootstrap correction with modified expected T-term equations.
evidence: Full text acquired; read abstract, introduction, general-design expected-T-term procedure and scope. For any random-model balanced design and bootstrap sampling plan; solves modified T-term equations for unbiased component estimates. Unbiased point estimates alone do not prove correct joint covariance, error-variance SE or coefficient CI coverage.
acquisition_note: November 2006 detailed 49-page report; paired with 2007 EPM paper. Acquisition validated by scripts/acquire.py; source sidecar contains timestamp, bytes and SHA-256.

title: Improved Confidence Interval Estimation for Variance Components and Error Variances in Generalizability Theory
relevance: GT-specific adaptation of modified-large-sample intervals to signed EMS combinations and error variances.
evidence: Full text acquired; read conceptual restrictions, proposed methods, simulation conclusions, D-study example and bibliography. Balanced all-random normal models. Person/item components involve differences of EMS; naive nonnegative-combination Satterthwaite formula has inappropriate premises. Paper reports accurate/conservative two-sided and upper-error bounds in tested designs.
acquisition_note: AERA April 1998 conference paper 11 PDFpages. Lu 1988 bibliography page range in this paper conflicts with Crossref (actual 35–43); source catalogue uses DOI metadata. Acquisition validated by scripts/acquire.py; source sidecar contains timestamp, bytes and SHA-256.

title: A Monte Carlo Study of Confidence Interval Methods for Generalizability Coefficient
relevance: Direct coefficient coverage comparison; particularly important scope/terminology traps.
evidence: Full HTML acquired; read model/resampling methods, simulation design, results, discussion and footnote. Study explicitly focuses ABSOLUTE error despite G title (therefore Phi). Four LMM techniques,1000 replications×500 bootstrap draws for 100×20×2 crossed/nested normal/binary/polytomous responses. Spherical-random-effects PB best; nested polytomous coverage about 81% at nominal 95%. Variance-component follow-up 18 conditions.
acquisition_note: Online 2021, EPM 82(4)705–718 issue 2022. Publisher PDF 403 and PMC PDF access page; public PMC HTML genuine full text acquired. All equations require preserved HTML/MathML or visual checking. Acquisition validated by scripts/acquire.py; source sidecar contains timestamp, bytes and SHA-256.

title: Which method is optimal for estimating variance components and their variability in generalizability theory? Evidence from a set of unified rules for bootstrap method
relevance: Open primary modern simulation synthesizing component-specific bootstrap rules.
evidence: Full text acquired; read simulation design, distributions, estimator descriptions, criteria, Tables 1–6, discussion and references. Four types of 100×20 p×i data,1000 trials;80%interval coverage with 25%relative-percent-bias acceptance rule. Recommends boot-p for persons,boot-pi/item,boot-i/interaction. This tolerance permits 0.60–1.00 coverage for nominal 0.80, so accurate-label is not strict calibration. No full crossed/nested G/Phi coverage theorem.
acquisition_note: Original title says form; title-only correction 2025 retained alongside paper. Acquisition validated by scripts/acquire.py; source sidecar contains timestamp, bytes and SHA-256.
